paragraphs.S03.C000.P000: By morning, the rain had thinned to a fine mist. Alice woke before her alarm and found the sitting room empty. On the table lay a map with a note from Eric: “Forecast changed. Þingvellir after ten. Breakfast before nine. Coffee on the left.”
paragraphs.S03.C000.P001: A jar of instant coffee stood on the right.
paragraphs.S03.C000.P002: Alice smiled and called her editor.
paragraphs.S03.C000.P003: “You made it?” Marina asked instead of saying hello.
paragraphs.S03.C000.P004: “Yes. I've spoken to all three participants. There's something you need to know about one of them.”
paragraphs.S03.C000.P005: Alice ran a finger along the edge of the map.
paragraphs.S03.C000.P007: Marina was silent for a moment.
paragraphs.S03.C000.P010: “Then it stays out. An ex isn't a genre. I need people, not a coincidence for the cover.”
paragraphs.S03.C000.P011: Alice felt relieved and irritated at the same time.
paragraphs.S03.C000.P012: “You can profile someone else instead,” Marina said. “An honest piece matters more to me.”
paragraphs.S03.C000.P013: “I'll keep him for now. If I can't separate the interview from the personal history, I'll tell you.”
paragraphs.S03.C000.P014: “Agreed. I want the opening paragraph on the evening of day four, like we discussed yesterday. Not the whole piece.”
paragraphs.S03.C000.P015: Alice opened yesterday's notes. She did not have a title yet, but she had a first question to carry forward.

paragraphs.S03.C001.P000: She circled yesterday's line about the way each of them had held the silence after Damir's answer. Marina did not need a conclusion yet. Alice wanted to see whether it would hold on the road, once they were all tired.

paragraphs.S03.C002.P000: She checked the name of the roadside café and the distance to the next one. Marina had asked for portraits of people, but Alice wanted to reveal them through the places that forced them out of their habits.

S03.C003.title: If S02-C1 is C — own choice

paragraphs.S03.C003.P000: She wrote down Damir's answer word for word and separated it with a line from the interview material for her editor. He had not given her permission to use it in the interview material. For now, keeping her promise mattered more than securing a good quote.

paragraphs.S03.C004.P000: Damir came into the sitting room carrying two cups.
paragraphs.S03.C004.P001: “I didn't expect to find you here this early,” he said.
paragraphs.S03.C004.P002: “Neither did I. We only have one kitchen.”
paragraphs.S03.C004.P003: He set one cup on the far edge of the table without sliding it toward her.
paragraphs.S03.C004.P005: “If you want it. Black, with a little milk on the side.”
paragraphs.S03.C004.P006: He still remembered. Alice could have been angry at memory, but memory had asked neither of them for permission.
paragraphs.S03.C004.P007: “You have all three weeks off?” Alice asked.
paragraphs.S03.C004.P008: “Until the end of the month. After my last contract. If I sign the next one, I won't have this much time again. I decided to see the place they're asking me to live in, not just the place they're asking me to work.”
paragraphs.S03.C004.P010: He sat in the chair by the window. Not beside her.
paragraphs.S03.C004.P011: “I didn't mean to make your work difficult,” he said.
paragraphs.S03.C004.P012: “You already have. Just not on purpose.”
paragraphs.S03.C004.P013: Damir accepted the answer, though Alice could tell by the way he held his cup that he wanted to argue.

S03.C005.title: If Alice sat beside Damir in S01-C1

paragraphs.S03.C005.P000: “It was easier in the car yesterday,” he said.
paragraphs.S03.C005.P001: “We could look out the window. Here we have to decide what to talk about.”
paragraphs.S03.C005.P002: He nodded and moved the second cup closer to her. Alice picked it up herself.

S03.C006.title: If Alice sat with Eric or Nick in S01-C1

paragraphs.S03.C006.P000: “I didn't ask you to talk in private yesterday,” Damir said.
paragraphs.S03.C006.P002: He was about to add something, but a door slammed in the hall. Alice took the cup and did not ask him to continue.

paragraphs.S03.C007.P000: Damir smiled. Alice did too, just a little. The awkwardness did not disappear, but it stopped taking up the whole room.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P001: After breakfast, they had forty minutes before departure. Nick went to find an adapter, Eric checked the car, and Damir went upstairs for his jacket. Alice decided to walk one block toward the harbor and discovered that Damir was heading the same way—not after her, but toward the pharmacy on the corner.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P005: “We have three weeks of bad route coincidences ahead of us.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P006: They stopped beside each other at a traffic light. The street was almost empty; the rain hung in the air without falling.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P007: “Did you tell your editor?” Damir asked.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P010: “She said an ex isn't a genre.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P012: “Give her time. She may still ask for your medical records as a sidebar.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P013: Damir smiled, then grew more serious.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P014: “If you don't want to write about me, I'll understand.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P015: “I'm supposed to write about all three participants.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P016: “Then I could answer in writing only.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P020: The words came out sharper than she intended. The light turned green. They crossed without continuing.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P021: By the water, gulls were fighting over a paper bag. Alice stopped to watch. So did Damir.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P022: “I didn't choose the job because it mattered more than you,” he said. “I chose the option where I didn't have to risk being told no.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P025: He did not defend himself. It made anger harder to hold on to.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P026: “I don't want to go through this now,” Alice said.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P028: “And don't expect the trip to fix everything.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P030: One gull tore the bag free and took off. The other remained on the pavement, shrieking after it in outrage.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P033: “Don't you dare defuse this conversation with a gull.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P034: “Too late. It makes a convincing case.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P035: They reached the pharmacy. Damir bought bandages and motion-sickness medicine for the group, though no one had asked him to.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P036: “Now that is still an old habit,” Alice said.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P039: He looked at the things he had bought.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P041: She expected an explanation of why bandages were objectively useful. Instead, Damir actually turned back toward the register.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P042: “No. Just ask later if they should go in the shared pack.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P044: Outside, he handed her the receipt.
paragraphs.S03.C007.P046: “You're a journalist. You may need evidence of my progress.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P047: “So far, it's evidence that you bought bandages.”
paragraphs.S03.C007.P049: They returned to the guesthouse separately. Damir stopped at a coffee shop and Alice walked on. It was almost meaningless, but she liked that he understood why those twenty meters mattered.

S03.C008.title: Choice S03-C1 — how will Alice end the conversation with Damir after the pharmacy?

S03.C009.title: A. Send him a short message

paragraphs.S03.C009.P000: At the entrance, Alice texted Damir: “Thank you for not continuing the conversation by the water.” His reply came while she was taking off her wet shoes: “Thank you too. See you by the car.” She did not try to decide what that was supposed to mean.

S03.C010.title: B. Let the walk end there

paragraphs.S03.C010.P000: Alice put her phone in her pocket. She wanted to remember the walk separately from everything else. When Damir came to the group dinner, she greeted him as another member of the group, and it did not feel like pretending.
